title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Technology Dispute Cases

articles.content_en:
II. Procedures for Handling Technology Contract Dispute Cases
7. After a technology contract dispute arises, a party may apply for arbitration to the agreed arbitration institution in accordance with the arbitration clause stipulated in the contract or a written arbitration agreement reached afterwards. The arbitration clause or arbitration agreement must specify the name of the arbitration institution and the matters to be submitted to arbitration. The People's Court shall not accept a technology contract dispute in which an arbitration clause or arbitration agreement is stipulated, except where such arbitration clause or arbitration agreement is invalid.
8. Where an arbitration clause or arbitration agreement agreed upon by the parties to a contract falls under any of the following circumstances, such arbitration clause or arbitration agreement shall be invalid:
(1) It fails to specify the specific name of the arbitration institution;
(2) It stipulates both applying to an arbitration institution for arbitration and filing a lawsuit with the People's Court;
(3) The institution agreed for arbitration is not a statutory technology contract arbitration institution.
For a technology contract with an invalid arbitration clause or arbitration agreement, the parties may reach a new written arbitration agreement; if they cannot reach a new written arbitration agreement, the parties may directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court having jurisdiction.
9. Where one party fails to perform an arbitral award made by an arbitration institution, the other party may apply for enforcement to the People's Court having jurisdiction, and the People's Court shall enforce it according to law.
Pursuant to Article 217 of the Civil Procedure Law, if the arbitral award of an arbitration institution is ruled by the People's Court not to be enforced, the parties may reapply for arbitration in accordance with the written arbitration agreement reached between them; or they may directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court.
10. Mediation agreements made by the competent department for technology contracts, relevant business competent departments, and intermediary institutions in accordance with Article 117 of the Implementing Regulations of the Technology Contract Law concerning technology contract disputes or disputes over the ownership of technological achievements shall be voluntarily performed by the parties. If one party fails to perform, the other party may apply for arbitration in accordance with the arbitration clause in the contract or a written arbitration agreement reached afterwards. If there is no arbitration clause or arbitration agreement, either party may file a lawsuit with the People's Court.
11. In a lawsuit over a technology contract dispute, if a third party claims ownership of the technological achievements under the contract, and if the disputed technological achievements only involve the right to use or transfer of non-patented technological achievements, the People's Court hearing the case may combine such ownership dispute with the contract dispute for trial. If the disputed technological achievements involve the right to apply for a patent or the patent right, the third party shall be informed to file a separate lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court having jurisdiction or request mediation by the patent administrative authority; after the ownership dispute is accepted as a separate case, the People's Court hearing the technology contract dispute case shall suspend the proceedings according to law, and resume the technology contract dispute proceedings after the ownership dispute is resolved.
12. In a lawsuit over a dispute concerning a patent exploitation license contract, if the licensee (licensee) or a third party requests the Patent Reexamination Board to declare the patent right invalid, the People's Court may not suspend the trial of the patent exploitation license contract case. If the patent right is declared invalid during the lawsuit for the contract dispute, it shall be handled in accordance with Article 50 of the Patent Law.
13. For a mixed contract primarily containing technology contract content but also including economic contract content, if the arbitration clause or arbitration agreement has no other special provisions regarding the scope of arbitration, and the arbitration institution makes an award jointly on disputes arising from such contract that have economic contract content, if a party applies for enforcement to the People's Court having jurisdiction, the People's Court shall enforce it according to law.

III. Determination of Causes of Action for Technology Contract Disputes
14. Where a party combines the contents of a technology contract and an economic contract into a single contract, or combines the contents of different types of technology contracts into one contract, the nature and cause of action of the case shall be determined based on the content of the rights and obligations in dispute between the parties, and the corresponding laws and regulations shall apply.
15. Where the name of a contract concluded by the parties is inconsistent with the rights and obligations stipulated in the contract, the type and cause of action of the contract shall be determined according to the content of the rights and obligations agreed in the contract, and the corresponding laws and regulations shall apply.
16. For a technology contract that transfers phased technological achievements and stipulates obligations for subsequent development, if the dispute arises concerning the effect of repeated testing of such phased achievements, it shall be handled as a technology transfer contract dispute; if the dispute arises concerning subsequent development, it may be handled as a technology development contract dispute, and the liability for breach of contract and the risk liability for subsequent development shall be identified and distinguished.
17. Where a technology transfer contract stipulates that the transferor shall provide relevant technical consulting or technical services to the transferee, such provisions shall be part of the technology transfer contract. When a dispute arises under such a contract, the cause of action shall be determined as a technology transfer contract dispute.
18. Where a technology transfer contract stipulates that the transferor shall provide specialized equipment or raw materials for implementing the technology to the transferee, such clauses shall be deemed as part of the technology transfer contract. When a dispute arises during the performance of the technology contract, the cause of action shall be determined as a technology transfer contract dispute.
19. Where a technology transfer contract includes the transferor's responsibility for exclusive sales of products manufactured by the transferee using the technology under the contract, if the dispute arises solely because the transferor fails or cannot fully perform the exclusive sales obligation and does not involve technical issues, the cause of action shall be determined as a purchase and sale contract dispute or a consignment contract dispute based on the content of the rights and obligations stipulated in the exclusive sales clause.
20. Where a joint venture contract is concluded in the form of technology investment, and the technology investor does not participate in the management and operation of the joint venture, and stipulates in the form of a guaranteed bottom-line clause that the joint venture shall pay technology usage fees, such joint venture contract shall be deemed a technology transfer contract, and the cause of action shall be determined as a technology transfer contract dispute.
21. For a contract concluded in the form of technology contracting, the type of contract shall be determined based on the nature and content of the contracted project. A contract with the development, transfer, consulting or service of technology as the contracted content shall be a technology contract.
22. For a dispute case involving computer software, if it is a dispute over software development, licensing or transfer contract, it shall be handled in accordance with the Technology Contract Law; if it is an infringement dispute, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Copyright Law and the Regulations on the Protection of Computer Software.

IV. Confirmation of the Validity of Technology Contracts
23. The People's Court, in handling a technology contract dispute case accepted by it, shall examine and confirm whether the technology contract is established and valid.
24. The examination and confirmation of the validity of a technology contract shall be carried out in accordance with Article 21 of the Technology Contract Law and Article 25 of the Implementing Regulations of the Technology Contract Law, and the technology contract shall not be confirmed invalid on any of the following grounds:
(1) The technology subject matter of the contract has not undergone technical evaluation;
(2) The technology developed or transferred, or the consulting opinions or technical service achievements provided, do not meet the conditions stipulated in the contract;
(3) The economic benefits generated by the performance of the technology contract do not reach the economic indicators stipulated in the contract;
(4) The technology contract has not been registered or filed with the relevant authorities, except where a contract for the transfer of a patent right or the right to apply for a patent must be registered and announced by the Patent Office;
(5) A patent exploitation license contract is concluded using technology that has been applied for a patent but has not yet been granted a patent right.
25. A technology contract concluded by an authorized agent beyond the scope of authorization with a third party, or concluded in the agent's own name with a third party, shall not be binding on the principal, except where the principal ratifies or participates in the performance.
26. A contract for the further transfer by the transferee of the technology obtained under a non-patented technology transfer contract or a patent exploitation license contract shall be invalid; however, if the contract stipulates that the transferee is permitted to further transfer, the further transfer contract shall be valid.
27. The conclusion, modification and rescission of a technology contract shall be in writing. Where a technology contract is concluded between the parties through correspondence, telegram, facsimile or similar means, and the main rights and obligations agreed upon by both parties are clear, the contract shall be deemed established.
28. An oral technology contract does not meet the formality requirements stipulated in the Technology Contract Law. Unless the oral technology contract has been performed and the parties have no dispute over the content of the main rights and obligations agreed orally, or such content can be confirmed through relevant evidence, in which case the technology contract may be deemed established, the oral technology contract shall be deemed not established.
29. Where laws or regulations require that product technology be submitted for approval by the relevant authorities or that a production license be obtained before production, the party implementing such product technology shall have the obligation to go through the approval procedures and obtain the production license. If, at the time of concluding the technology transfer contract, the parties have not yet gone through the approval procedures or obtained the production license, they shall do so retroactively, and the validity of the contract shall not be affected by such retroactive procedures; if they fail to do so in a timely manner, they shall cease production or implementation of such technology.
30. Where a technology contract contains clauses concerning the provision of relevant samples, prototypes, specialized equipment, specialized raw materials or products for the purpose of performing the obligations under the technology contract, whether the parties to the contract have such business scope shall not affect the validity of the technology contract.

V. Handling of Invalid Technology Contracts
31. After a technology contract is performed, it is impossible to restore the status quo ante the conclusion of the contract according to the principle of restitution. Once a technology contract is confirmed invalid, an analysis and handling shall be made, in light of the characteristics of technology contracts and specific circumstances such as the causes of and liabilities for the invalidity, regarding the losses suffered by the parties in terms of competitive advantages and economic interests as a result of the invalidity of the contract.
32. After a technology contract is confirmed invalid, it may be handled in accordance with the following principles:
(1) For economic losses caused by the invalidity of the technology contract, in accordance with the principle of fault liability, the party liable for the invalidity of the contract shall compensate the losses suffered by the other party due to such invalidity; if both parties are at fault for the invalidity of the contract, each shall bear corresponding liability.
(2) If the research and development party, transferor, consultant or service provider of the technology contract has performed the obligations stipulated in the contract, and the liability for the invalidity of the contract lies with the other party, the research and development funds, technology usage fees and remuneration for consulting services that such party is entitled to collect under the contract may be deemed as compensation for the economic losses suffered by it due to the invalidity of the contract caused by the other party's fault; the amount already collected shall not be returned, and the amount not yet paid shall be paid in full. If the liability for the invalidity of the contract lies with the aforementioned research and development party, transferor, consultant or service provider, the fees already collected shall be returned in full to the other party, and compensation shall be paid for the economic losses caused to the other party due to the invalidity of the contract.
(3) Technical materials, samples, prototypes, etc. received under the technology contract shall be returned to the right holder, and no copies of the relevant technical materials shall be retained; if non-patented technological achievements are involved, the transferee shall have a duty of confidentiality and shall not use or transfer such non-patented technological achievements without authorization.
33. If a technology contract lacks legal binding force because it does not meet the statutory formality requirements or lacks the required procedures for approval, registration or announcement, and both parties wish to continue performance, they shall perfect the formality requirements or retroactively complete the relevant procedures for approval, registration and announcement.
34. Where a technology contract is confirmed invalid due to infringement of the lawful rights and interests of others, it shall be handled in accordance with Article 28 of the Implementing Regulations of the Technology Contract Law and the following principles:
(1) After a technology contract is confirmed invalid due to infringement of another person's patent right, patent application right or patent exploitation right, if the contract has not been performed, it shall not be performed; if it is being performed, performance shall be terminated. The party providing the technology shall bear liability for the infringement; if the party receiving the technology, knowing that the other party is infringing, still concludes and performs the contract with it, it shall be deemed joint infringement and bear joint and several liability.
(2) After a technology contract is confirmed invalid due to infringement of the right to use or transfer non-patented technological achievements, the party providing the technology shall bear liability for the infringement. A party that has in good faith received such non-patented technological achievements may continue to implement such technology, but shall pay reasonable royalties to the right holder. If the party receiving the technology, knowing that the other party is infringing, still concludes and performs the contract with it, it shall be deemed joint infringement and bear joint and several liability, and shall not continue to implement such non-patented technology.
(3) For a contract that infringes upon another person's rights of invention, discovery, or other scientific and technological achievements such as honorary rights, if the invalidation of the relevant clauses does not affect the validity of the remaining part, the remaining part shall continue to be valid. The party liable for the infringement may, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, be ordered by the People's Court to cease the infringement, eliminate the adverse effects and compensate for losses in accordance with Article 118 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China.

VI. Liability for Breach of Technology Contracts
35. The obligations of the parties to perform a technology contract and the liability for breach of contract shall be based on the scope agreed upon in the contract terms. The predictions and analyses concerning economic benefits or cost indicators in the feasibility analysis report prepared by the parties when concluding a technology contract shall not be deemed as the acceptance criteria agreed in the contract, unless the contract specifically provides otherwise.
36. To determine whether a party to a technology contract has properly performed the contract, a judgment shall be made on whether the party has completed the agreed obligations in the agreed manner and met the acceptance criteria within the validity period of the contract. Errors that can be timely corrected, necessary technical adjustments made by a party in technical details or to adapt to changes in circumstances, which do not affect the performance of contractual obligations, shall not constitute a breach of contract.
37. In a technology transfer contract, the transferor's basic obligation is to ensure that the transferee implements the technology in the agreed manner and achieves the technical indicators agreed in the contract. Unless the contract clearly stipulates that the transferor shall participate in the transferee's operation and management or guarantee that the transferee will achieve the expected economic benefits, the transferor shall not bear liability for the transferee's implementation of the technology and the economic benefits after production.
38. In performing a technology contract, the delivery of technical drawings, materials, samples, and other material technical conditions for providing technical achievements or consulting services shall be consistent with the contract terms. If it is discovered that relevant technical drawings, materials, etc., are inconsistent with the contract terms, they shall be promptly corrected and supplemented. If the correction or supplementation of relevant technical drawings, materials, or data causes economic losses or additional burdens to the other party, it shall be treated as improper performance of the contract, except in the following circumstances:
(1) The technical improvement is approved by the other party or made at the request of the other party;
(2) The contract contains provisions on subsequent improvements, and the improvement made by one party falls within the scope of contractual performance;
(3) The contract stipulates that the party providing the technology has the right to adjust the technical scheme according to local conditions, and the adjustment is made with sufficient reasons;
(4) The technical improvement made by one party results in more positive and favorable effects on the performance of the technology contract than the original technology contract.
39. If the transferor of an exclusive exploitation license contract does not have the conditions to exploit its patent technology and cooperates with another entity to exploit the patent technology, or exploits the patent technology through technology contribution as equity participation or joint operation, it may be deemed as the transferor's own exploitation of the patent technology and shall not be treated as a breach of contract. However, if the transferor cooperates with multiple entities or contributes the same patent technology to multiple equity participations or joint operations, it shall be treated as a breach of contract. Whether the transferee of an exclusive exploitation license may cooperate with others or use the licensed patent technology as equity participation or joint operation shall be determined by the contract; if the contract does not provide otherwise, the transferee shall not cooperate with others or use the licensed patent technology as equity participation or joint operation.
40. The research and development party of a technology development contract shall not conclude separate commissioned development contracts with two or more (including two) commissioning parties for the same research and development subject, nor charge duplicate research and development fees. If the research and development party concludes two or more contracts for the same research and development subject, the first contract shall be valid, and the subsequent contracts shall be void. The research and development party that repeatedly signs contracts shall bear liability for the invalidity of the contracts.
41. If a technology contract stipulates liquidated damages, after one party breaches the contract, it shall pay the agreed liquidated damages to the other party regardless of whether the other party has suffered losses as a result; unless otherwise specially agreed in the contract, no additional compensation shall be made for the other party's losses.
The parties to a technology contract may specially agree in the contract that if one party breaches the contract and the agreed liquidated damages are insufficient to compensate the other party for the losses incurred, the breaching party shall compensate for the losses and make up the shortfall in the liquidated damages.
42. If a technology transfer contract does not stipulate the method for calculating liquidated damages and compensation for losses, the compensation amount shall be calculated based on the actual losses caused by the breaching party to the other party. If the transferor breaches the contract, the transferee's actual losses shall include the technology usage fees and remuneration already paid, as well as actual losses incurred during the implementation of the technology. If the transferee breaches the contract, the transferor's actual losses shall include the technology usage fees receivable under the contract and actual losses incurred during the performance of the technology contract. When calculating actual losses, the compensation amount shall be determined in accordance with the principle of reasonable compensation.
43. If a technology transfer contract stipulates that the technology acquired by the transferee must undergo small-scale testing, pilot-scale testing, or industrial testing before being put into batch production, the transferor shall not bear liability for losses incurred by the transferee due to directly putting the technology into batch production without such testing.
44. In a contract for the transfer of stage-specific technological achievements, the parties may agree on the method of bearing the risk liability that may arise from directly applying such stage-specific technological achievements to industrial production. In the event of risk failure, the risk liability shall be handled in accordance with the contract.
45. The following acts of breach by one party may be deemed as rendering the performance of the contract unnecessary or impossible for the other party:
(1) The breach causes severe damage to the material and technical conditions necessary for contract performance, which cannot be remedied within the validity period of the contract.
(2) The subject matter or technology under the contract has significant defects, and after scientific demonstration and analysis, the expected technical indicators cannot be achieved.

VII. Handling Disputes over Ownership of Technological Achievements
46. The ownership of technological achievements completed by scientific and technical personnel during their spare-time or part-time activities shall be confirmed in accordance with the agreements in the technology contract concluded with the employing entity, unless such agreements infringe upon the technological rights and interests of others. If the contract does not provide for such ownership, it shall be confirmed by reference to the provisions of Article 6 of the Technology Contract Law.
47. The term "duties of the current position" as used in Article 4 of the Implementing Regulations of the Technology Contract Law refers to the work tasks and scope of responsibility of the employee's position as stipulated by the entity. If the work tasks and scope of responsibility of the employee's position have no direct relationship with the research and development of a particular technological achievement, and the employee completes the technological achievement using professional knowledge, experience, and information while fulfilling the duties of the current position, such technological achievement shall not be deemed as "performing the duties of the current position."
48. The term "mainly utilizing the material and technical conditions of the entity" as used in Article 6 of the Technology Contract Law means that, during the process of completing the research and development of the technological achievement, the employee has used all or most of the entity's funds, equipment, facilities, or raw materials, or the substantive content of the technological achievement is completed on the basis of technological achievements, stage-specific achievements, or key technologies that have not yet been disclosed by the entity.
After the completion of the technological achievement, the use of material conditions for verification tests, small-scale tests, or pilot-scale tests on the technical scheme that do not include subsequent development content, or the use of technical information that has been disclosed to the public by the entity or is common knowledge to experts in the field during the research and development process, shall not constitute "mainly utilizing the material and technical conditions of the entity" as referred to in Article 6 of the Technology Contract Law.
49. If an employee, while fulfilling the duties of the current position, conducts self-directed research and development on a subject that is in competition with the entity, the employee shall reach a written agreement with the entity in advance on the scope of utilizing the entity's material and technical conditions, the method of compensation, and the ownership of the right to use, transfer, and apply for patents for the completed technological achievement. If a dispute over ownership arises, it shall be confirmed in accordance with the agreement.
50. A person who has made creative contributions to an invention-creation shall be the inventor or designer. When determining creative contributions, the substantive technical components of the invention-creation or scientific and technological achievement shall be broken down, and the person who proposes the substantive technical components and thus accomplishes the technical scheme shall be objectively and fairly identified as the person who has made creative contributions.

X. Technical Appraisal of the Subject Matter of Technology Contracts
59. In litigation of technology contract disputes, the appraisal of the technology involved in the technology contract shall take as the appraisal object the technological achievements or technical service content provided by the transferor, developer, or service provider as stipulated in the contract, and shall examine from aspects such as principles, design, process, and necessary technical data, in accordance with the testing methods and acceptance criteria agreed in the contract, whether the said technology can achieve the technical and economic indicators stipulated in the contract.
60. If the parties have not agreed on the acceptance criteria in the technology contract, and there are no national standards or professional technical standards for appraisal, experts may be organized to render an evaluation conclusion on whether the technology involved in the technology contract meets the general practical requirements of the industry.
61. If the parties have not agreed on the testing methods or acceptance criteria in the technology contract and fail to reach an agreement thereafter, the People's Court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case, adopt testing methods and acceptance criteria prescribed by the industry, commonly used in the industry, or practically suitable for testing appraisal, expert evaluation, or acceptance appraisal. If the acceptance criteria stipulated in the contract are clear and the technological achievement is not complex, the appraisal of the technological achievement may be conducted through on-site demonstration, operation, or production by the parties.
62. In determining the appraisal institution for technological achievements, in addition to statutory appraisal units, the parties may negotiate and recommend an institution or expert mutually trusted for appraisal; if the parties cannot reach an agreement, the People's Court shall entrust an appraisal institution recommended by the relevant science and technology commission or retain an expert group composed of relevant experts for appraisal.
63. For technological achievements that have already passed appraisal in accordance with relevant state regulations or have been proven by production practice to be mature and reliable, if the parties to the contract dispute the evaluation of such technological achievements, the People's Court shall, after review, not conduct a repeat appraisal of the technological achievement, unless there is contrary evidence sufficient to negate the appraisal conclusion.
64. In disputes concerning patent exploitation license contracts, a patent certificate shall not be used as a substitute for the technical appraisal conclusion.
65. The appraisal of technological achievements shall be strictly carried out in accordance with Article 72 of the Civil Procedure Law. The appraisal department shall pay attention to comprehensively understanding the case materials necessary for the appraisal and question both parties; the opinions of individual experts on the technological achievement shall not be used as the appraisal conclusion.
April 2, 1995
